title: Tech Note: Hexadecimal Notation and Bitwise Operators in V6
author: Gordon Muirhead

historical_commentary.text: This note previews new 4D V6 (pre-release, 'Developer Release 1') language features: hexadecimal display formatting, bitwise operators (And, Or, Xor, Bit Test, Shift Left/Right), and the new BLOB data type, demonstrated via example methods for decoding raw bytes. The bitwise operators and BLOB data type introduced here became stable, long-lived parts of the 4D language and remain conceptually current, though BLOB manipulation in modern 4D is often superseded by more structured object/JSON handling for many use cases; the note's V6 pre-release caveats and pointer-symbol change are dated historical detail.
related_updates: The bitwise operators (&, |, ^|, ??, >>, <<) and hexadecimal display formats introduced in V6 remain part of the 4D language today essentially unchanged
The BLOB data type introduced in V6 is still supported, though modern 4D development often favors object (JSON-like) or ORDA-based data handling for many tasks BLOBs were historically used for

This note predates V6's official release (it explicitly discusses a pre-release 'Developer Release 1'), and the pointer symbol change ('->') it references was part of V6's broader language modernization
